svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The carbon cycle: carbon moves between the atmosphere, living things, the oceans and fossil fuels."], [1, "Photosynthesis: plants take in CO\u2082 and make carbon compounds."], [3, "Feeding: carbon passes to animals as they eat plants."], [5, "Respiration by plants and animals returns CO\u2082 to the air."], [7, "Death and decay: decomposers feed on dead material and respire, releasing CO\u2082."], [9.5, "Where decay is prevented, the carbon forms fossil fuels over millions of years."], [11.5, "Combustion of fossil fuels releases CO\u2082 quickly."], [13.5, "The oceans absorb CO\u2082, which dissolves in sea water."]]
svg.title: The carbon cycle
svg.desc: The carbon cycle: photosynthesis, feeding, respiration, death and decay, fossilisation, combustion and the oceans, with carbon atoms moving along each arrow.
svg.text: Black dots: carbon atoms moving through the cycle.

g.data-info: About 0.04% of the air. Removed by photosynthesis and dissolving in the oceans; added by respiration, decay and combustion.
Photosynthesis turns CO₂ into glucose and other carbon compounds. Plants also respire.
Get carbon compounds by feeding; release CO₂ in respiration.
Bacteria and fungi feed on dead organisms and waste, releasing CO₂ in respiration.
Coal, oil and gas formed over millions of years from organisms that did not decay (waterlogged, no oxygen).
CO₂ dissolves in sea water; some is used by marine organisms to make calcium carbonate shells, which can form limestone.
Burning fossil fuels and wood releases CO₂ quickly: the main cause of rising CO₂ levels.
